checks.label: In an exponential function the output is multiplied by the same factor every time the input increases by one: every multiplying bar and dot drawn, on every screen and at every slider setting, is the one before times its growth factor

The rate of growth is proportional to the current value: each rise or drop of the multiplying column is the same share of the bar before it, while the adding column rises by the same amount every step

The growth factor is larger than one when the growth rate is positive and less than one when it is negative: growing by a percentage gives a factor above one and a rising column, losing a percentage or halving gives one below and a falling column

Every number follows its rule: 21 and 1,024 at step 10 (slip 64); 72 from 48 (slips 49.5 and 96); £1,628.89 against £1,500, with 1.98 and 2.08 either side of double; £4,500 (slips £4,000 and £500); 50 V and 25 V; √2 ≈ 1.414; 300 (slips 450 and 500); 4, 2.25 and 1.78; 183 against 163, then 1,327, 370 and 455; 18.5 s; and each answer offered is the value its own working gives
Decay never reaches zero: halving from 400 V, every bar drawn stays above the bottom line and each drop is half the one before, and twelve halvings still leave more than nothing
Before an answer, nothing in a puzzle's picture gives it away, and a right answer shows it
Each puzzle offers three answers and takes only its right one, and every wrong answer has a hint of its own
Bars and dots are drawn to scale: each bar's height is its value on its screen's one scale, the tallest filling the frame, and each dot sits at its step and value
Half a step multiplies by the square root of the factor, because two half steps make one whole step: at × 2 the mark sits at √2, and at × 9 the right answer is 300, three times 100
Every demonstration has finished arriving within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion, right or wrong, within 2.5 s
